messages:
Hiro Tanaka: Kicking off kernel compare thread for H100 attention. We need a clear call on variant `attn_sm90_v3` vs current default (`v2`) for profile-pack v1.0. Please drop microbench numbers + any gotchas (seq len buckets, headroom, fallback behavior).

Grace Kim: I ran the microbench on `h100-sxm` (CUDA 12.4 / driver 550.54) with our `attn_bench.py` harness.

Config:
- model: llama-3-70b-instruct (fp16)
- bs: 1, 2, 4
- prefill: 128/512/2048/4096
- decode: 128 tokens
- kv cache: paged
- scheduler: single stream (so kernel dominates)

Headline: v3 is consistently better at longer prefill.

Results (tok/s decode, mean over 50 iters, bs=2):
```
prefill=128  v2=3900  v3=3950  (+1.3%)
prefill=512  v2=3650  v3=3780  (+3.6%)
prefill=2048 v2=3100  v3=3420  (+10.3%)
prefill=4096 v2=2520  v3=2900  (+15.1%)
```
Prefill latency p95 (ms, bs=2):
```
prefill=2048 v2=41.2  v3=37.0 (-10.2%)
prefill=4096 v2=86.5  v3=74.8 (-13.5%)
```
No correctness diffs spotted.

Yuki Sato: Nice. Any changes in scratch usage / reg pressure? I’m worried about perf cliff when we’re near memory headroom (mixed workloads + fragmentation).

Grace Kim: Good q. I logged SM occupancy from nsight compute; v3 slightly lower occupancy but better overall time (likely memory access pattern). Memory peak from `nvidia-smi dmon` looked basically unchanged (<1% diff) but I didn’t do deep allocator traces.

Isabella Rossi: I did a smaller sweep focusing on long-context edge. Same machine type (H100 SXM) but w/ concurrency=8 to simulate batching (still micro-ish).

v3 better until we hit *very* long prefill, then we start seeing fallback spikes due to our guard condition.

From logs (kernel_choice counts):
- prefill=8192, decode=128: v3 chosen ~92% of requests, ~8% fallback to v2
- prefill=16384, decode=128: v3 chosen ~35%, rest fallback

Not sure if that fallback is expected or too conservative.

Noah Patel: When fallback happens, do we see tail latency bumps or is it benign? The concern is jitter from switching kernels under load.

Isabella Rossi: There’s a bump in p99 when fallback rate > ~5%. It’s not massive but noticeable.

Example (concurrency=8, prefill=8192):
```
v2: p50=31ms p95=38ms p99=44ms
v3: p50=28ms p95=36ms p99=52ms   (p99 worse b/c fallback jitter)
```
When I force v3 only (disable fallback) p99 goes back down (but we risk the reason the fallback exists…)

Hiro Tanaka: That’s helpful. The current fallback is based on shared-mem scratch heuristic + seq len cap, right?

Grace Kim: Yeah, in the prototype branch we gate v3 when `max_seqlen > 8192` OR when `head_dim` is one of the oddball configs. For llama-like head_dim=128 it should be fine; for some Mistral variants we saw spills.

Omar El-Sayed: Reminder: once this lands in profile pack, we need kernel fallback counters exported (at least `kernel_choice` and `kernel_fallback_reason`). Otherwise oncall won’t be able to tell “p99 regressed because we’re falling back” vs scheduler.

Yuki Sato: +1. Also, can we make fallback deterministic per model-load instead of per request? If it flips per request it’s going to be gross for tail.

Noah Patel: Agree. Ideal: decide at model init based on detected GPU + driver + compiled kernel availability + model config. Per-request should only be for *hard* safety checks.

Grace Kim: We can do “sticky” selection: evaluate once when loading model (or first request) and set `active_attn_kernel = v3|v2`, with per-request fallback only on runtime error / unusual seqlen. That would reduce jitter.

Marcus Reed: For benchmark-lab gating, I’d prefer sticky selection so the numbers are stable across runs.

Hiro Tanaka: Ok. Isabella—can you share the exact harness cmd + env? Want to replicate on our side.

Isabella Rossi: Sure.

Command:
```
python3 tools/attn_bench.py \
  --model llama3-70b \
  --dtype fp16 \
  --prefill_lens 512,2048,4096,8192,16384 \
  --decode_len 128 \
  --batch_size 2 \
  --concurrency 8 \
  --iters 200 \
  --warmup 50 \
  --kernel v2,v3 \
  --log_kernel_choice
```
Env:
```
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0
CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS=1
NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1   # single GPU
```
I can paste raw csv if useful.

Grace Kim: Re: long seqlen, I can try tightening guard: v3 only up to 8192 for now in default profile, but allow override for eval. That’d still cover most of our workload buckets (I think 4k/8k buckets dominate for Hosted).

Noah Patel: For profile pack, that’s reasonable: safe default. But we need to document “for >8k context we may choose v2; expect lower tok/s, stable tail”.

Yuki Sato: Another detail: does v3 require a specific CUDA minor? I remember a PTX issue on 12.2.

Grace Kim: I saw that too. On 12.2 the compile path uses a different intrinsic and perf was worse + occasional miscompile (we disabled it in that environment). On 12.4 it’s solid.

So compatibility rule probably:
- H100 (sm90)
- CUDA >= 12.3 (prefer 12.4)
- driver >= 550 (or whatever we standardize)

Hiro Tanaka: Good, we can encode that in selection rules: `sku=H100` + `cuda>=12.3` -> allow v3.

Omar El-Sayed: Please include a clear log line at startup:
`active_profile=... kernel.attn=h100_v3 enabled=true reason=...`
We had too many “what kernel am I on?” pings last month.

Marcus Reed: Also: bench numbers for “mixed prompt lengths” matter more than single bucket. If we switch kernels based on seqlen per request, mixed workloads will thrash.

Yuki Sato: FWIW I ran a mixed distribution (prefill lens sampled {256,512,2k,8k} with weights 0.5/0.2/0.2/0.1, concurrency=16). v3 sticky on (<=8k) improved p95 by ~6% and p99 was flat. When per-request fallback enabled, p99 got worse by ~9%.

So: sticky selection + conservative max seqlen threshold seems like the right combo.

Grace Kim: That aligns with my intuition. I can update the branch to:
- Decide kernel at model load
- Only fallback on “seq len > max_supported” OR runtime error
- Export `kernel_fallback_total{reason=...}`

Hiro Tanaka: Please do. Also add a note in the PR about why we’re not doing per-request selection (tail stability).

Isabella Rossi: One more: v3 seems to prefer `--use_flash_prefill=true` path; when disabled, gains shrink to ~2-3% even at 4k. Not sure if that’s expected or just how the harness is wired.

Noah Patel: That’s important because scheduler can force different prefill mode depending on batching. Let’s make sure the bench harness mimics production flags.

Marcus Reed: I can run on benchmark-lab config once Grace lands the sticky change. I’ll add it to the H100 matrix: baseline (v2) vs candidate (v3) across bucketed workloads.

Omar El-Sayed: If anyone sees OOM/alloc spikes with v3, ping me. I can add extra allocator counters around prefill to see if it’s indirectly changing fragmentation patterns.

Hiro Tanaka: Action items:
- Grace: update kernel selection to sticky + compat gate (cuda/driver) + counters.
- Isabella: share csv + note on flash prefill coupling.
- Marcus: rerun matrix once patch is in.

We’ll target enabling v3 by default for H100 in profile-pack v1.0 if p99 is non-regressing under mixed workloads.

Grace Kim: ack, I’ll push an update today and link here.

Yuki Sato: :thumbsup: (also please ensure Dedicated can pin v2 if a customer is on older driver; support is already asking)

Hiro Tanaka: Yep, will be part of override story. Keeping this thread open for more numbers.
